scenarios.name: decayed-attacker-is-sacrificed-at-end-of-combat-not-on-attack
scenarios.why: Rot-Curse Rakshasa is a 5/5 with Trample and Decayed. Its triggered half says: when it attacks, sacrifice it at END of combat. It attacks here (unblocked, 5 trample to the defender), and it is still on the battlefield tapped right after the declaration; only at end of combat is it sacrificed to the graveyard.

scenarios.name: decayed-creature-cannot-block
scenarios.why: Decayed's static half means the decayed creature itself cannot block. Here p0's Grizzly Bears attacks; p1's Grizzly Bears is a legal blocker (so the blockers decision is posed) but p1's Rot-Curse Rakshasa, which has Decayed, is not a legal block.
